card.name: Saidi
card.era: ancient roots; staged female cane form from the 1960s
card.tagline: Upper Egyptian cane dance born from stick combat
card.profile: Saidi (raqs al-assaya, 'cane dance') is a folk dance of the Sa'id - Upper Egypt - performed to the strong, earthy Saidi rhythm on mizmar, rebaba and tabla. Per New York Folklore, it has two strands: the men's martial tahtib with a heavy stick, and the women's raqs al-assaya, in which a lighter, often decorated cane is twirled and balanced, with bouncy footwork echoing Upper Egypt's prized horses. The staged female version was popularised by the choreographer Mahmoud Reda and his national troupe.
card.insight: Saidi is the principal cane dance of Egyptian folklore and a staple of weddings and festivals; its female form theatricalises the masculine combat art of tahtib (New York Folklore; Wikipedia).
card.image_significance: Upper Egypt's earthy cane dance. A representative image shows a line or row formation, often with canes, swords or flowing veils — Upper Egypt (Sa'id), Egypt.
